caption: What if you fired a cannon from the top of Everest? It's Isaac Newton's famous cannonball thought experiment. Put the cannon on Everest, 8,849 m up, and pretend there's no air. Fire at 1 km/s and the ball falls for about 42 seconds, landing about 42 km away. Fast or slow, every ball drops about 5 metres in its first second. But Earth's surface curves down about 5 metres for every 8 km. So fire sideways at about 7.9 km/s, over 28,000 km/h, and the ground curves away as fast as the ball falls. That's an orbit. The ISS and every satellite stay up the same way: they're always falling around Earth. Fire at 11.2 km/s and the ball escapes Earth for good. In real life, air would slow and heat the ball. Plot twist: at orbit speed, about 84 minutes later the ball comes all the way round and hits your cannon from behind. Which speed would YOU pick? 👇
